units.title: Arbitrum Nitro and Orbit chains
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-996 and L-988. The cycle 22 census of PoolManager outflows (research/network-risk/cycles/022/theme-outflow-census.work, census3.py) skips the rows where a fault in arithmetic or settlement would show: native flows, transactions with a ModifyLiquidity, and amounts the PoolManager itself computed. The unlock stack scan of the same cycle (research/network-risk/cycles/022/theme-unlockless-frames.work/scripts) reconciled the PoolManager's native balance per transaction on four networks only. This theme checks what block producers wrote against the source, transaction by transaction. Task 1: for the networks that serve debug_traceTransaction with prestateTracer in diff mode, or trace_replayTransaction with stateDiff (try Ethereum, Base, Unichain, Arbitrum One, BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM, and record every refusal), take one window of at least 20,000 PoolManager transactions per network, newest first, with the window recorded. For each transaction fetch the PoolManager's storage and native balance before and after, and its Swap, ModifyLiquidity, Donate, Initialize and ERC-6909 Transfer logs. Task 2: recompute what the source owes from the state before the transaction. For a swap rerun Pool.swap with tools/opdiff/v4math.py and replay.py (tick bitmap words and liquidityNet read at the parent block). For a liquidity change recompute Pool.modifyLiquidity: the amounts from SqrtPriceMath, the fee growth inside the range, the fees owed, and the tick and bitmap writes. For a donate recompute the fee growth increase. Compare with the mined logs and with every PoolManager storage word the transaction wrote: slot0, liquidity, both fee growth globals, each tick's liquidityGross, liquidityNet and fee growth outside, bitmap words, position liquidity and fee growth snapshots, protocol fees accrued and ERC-6909 balances. A word that differs by even one unit is a mismatch. Task 3: per transaction, the change in the PoolManager's native balance must equal native settles minus native takes from the call trace, and for every ERC-20 with a ModifyLiquidity in the transaction the Transfer logs in and out must net to what the recomputed deltas, hook deltas and claims minted or burned allow. Task 4: report per network the transactions replayed, storage words compared, and every mismatch in full (hash, block, slot, expected, mined). Explain each mismatch from the source before calling it a fault: dynamic fee hooks, hook return deltas and protocol fees change amounts legitimately. Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM matter most, because their block producer is not the code that answers eth_call. If time remains (L-988), continue the census gaps named in the cycle 22 research file for Base, Robinhood Chain, Ethereum and X Layer.

HyperEVM headers carry no usable state root, and the public replica (nanoreth, commit b92ad36 behind rpc.hyperlend.finance in cycle 22) compares its own root with zero (finding F-120). The validator is closed. So a pool word that the validator computed differently from revm would raise no alarm anywhere; it would only leave the official endpoint and a replica answering differently. Task 1 (L-994): find the public endpoints that answer from the validator's own state (rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm) and from a re-execution (nanoreth replicas), and record web3_clientVersion for each. At one recent block that both hold, list every PoolManager storage slot written in the last 10,000 blocks. Take them from the logs: slot0, liquidity and fee growth of every pool with a Swap, ModifyLiquidity or Donate, the ticks and bitmap words those touched, position slots, ERC-6909 balances from Transfer logs and protocol fees accrued. Use research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/statekeys.py for the slot derivation; the PoolManager is 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F. Read each slot with eth_getStorageAt at that block on both kinds of endpoint, along with the PoolManager's native balance and the balanceOf of its ten largest currencies. Report slots compared and every difference in full. If the two endpoints cannot be pinned to one block, say so and compare at the nearest pair with the slots that changed in between removed. Task 2 (L-995): nanoreth nb-20261125-2 treats every transaction with gas price 0 as a system transaction and takes its sender from the low 20 bytes of the signature s value with no signature check (src/node/primitives/transaction.rs lines 47-97 and 182-184), and it switches off EIP-3607 and the base fee check in replay. Over the whole HyperEVM history, or the longest range public endpoints serve (record it), list every mined transaction with gas price 0 and group by decoded sender and by target. Is any sender other than 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 and the 0x20-prefixed token system addresses? Is any target the PoolManager, or a token contract with the PoolManager as transfer source? Do the Hyperliquid documents say that a user transaction can never be mined with gas price 0? Task 3 (L-1002): read the aligned quote asset documents and the API reference again for which signature authorises the treasury rebalance of a linked contract and whether it can name a sender other than the registered treasury address. This would settle finding F-020.

An ordinary account that can place code there gets the callbacks of a pool that other accounts already use: with the return delta flags it takes part of every swap or removal (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:248-315, 232-243), and it is the only caller for which callbacks are skipped (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:171-175). Start with 0xf8c3f4243c4d8c02831a718a7978fd869f094300 (pools with third-party positions on Polygon and Avalanche) and 0x4cd3be87...c0cc (CreateX output, code on Base, a third-party position on OP Mainnet). Task 4: the reverse case. Analysis only: deploy nothing and send no transactions; test by eth_call with state overrides where a network supports them.

Cycle 22 found that celo-reth v1.0.10 lets a negative gas refund counter reach revm's set_final_refund, which casts it to u64 and caps it, so the transaction gets the largest refund (finding F-144). It is information level on Celo because the refund is gas only. The same kind of fault matters more where the fee or its refund is a token flow from a custody account, since a wrapped value then moves tokens. Task 1: at the builds the endpoints report today, read the fee charge, refund and reimbursement code of every client that has its own handler for it: Base (reth v2.5.2 base v1.5.6, and v1.6.0-rc.1 with its EIP-8130 phase loop), X Layer (xlayer v0.0.7, post_exec_settlement_deltas and gasless system calls), Tempo at a9d6748 and the T14 tag (fee token collection and refund through the fee manager and its AMM), mega-evm v1.7.4 (storage gas and resource refunds), Arc v0.8.6 (fees in the native USDC), Celo (fee currency debit and credit under CIP-64 and CIP-66), Monad (charge on gas limit, reserve balance) and HyperEVM. For each, quote the lines where the amount is computed, name the integer types and every cast, and say whether a signed, wrapped or truncated value can reach a balance write. Task 2: for each, name the account that pays a refund or receives a fee, and say whether an ordinary account can make the PoolManager that account or make the flow touch a token balance the PoolManager holds. On Tempo the PoolManager is 0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029 and fees are paid in TIP-20 tokens it may hold. Task 3: where a path looks reachable, test it read-only: eth_call, eth_estimateGas or eth_simulateV1 with state overrides, comparing the fee the network reports for a mined transaction of that shape with what the source computes. Find mined transactions of the Celo shape (a CIP-64 transaction whose main call refills the debited slot) and check their receipts against the wrapped refund. Task 4: say whether any of these paths changes a value that the PoolManager reads inside a call: msg.value, a balance it reads between sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364), or gas forwarded to a hook or a token.
